Problem: Given plane alpha parallel plane beta, m subset alpha, n subset beta. Which conclusion necessarily correct?
Options:
A. m,n are parallel lines
B. m,n are skew lines (异面直线)
C. m,n are coplanar lines (共面直线)
D. m,n are non-intersecting lines (不相交直线)

We have two parallel distinct planes? Usually 平面α // 平面β means parallel planes, likely distinct (no intersection). Lines m in alpha, n in beta. Since planes are parallel, lines in separate parallel planes cannot intersect (if they intersected, point in both planes, impossible). So they are non-intersecting. Non-intersecting lines in 3D can be parallel or skew. Are they necessarily non-intersecting: yes. Not necessarily parallel: if directions differ, skew. Not necessarily skew: if directions parallel, they are parallel lines (in parallel planes), which are coplanar? Parallel lines are coplanar (there exists a plane containing both). Option C says coplanar lines. Are any two non-parallel non-intersecting lines skew, not coplanar. Since directions can be nonparallel -> skew, not coplanar. So C not necessarily. B not necessarily because can be parallel. D yes: 不相交直线 means non-intersecting lines, includes parallel and skew. In Chinese high school, 异面直线 are non-coplanar non-intersecting; parallel lines are non-intersecting but coplanar. Thus D always true.

它们可能是平行直线，也可能是异面直线，因此一定正确的是“不相交直线”。

答案：D
